question: Money multiplier can be expressed as ______.

options.text: Statutory liquidity ratio / Cash Reserve Ratio
Cash reserve ratio – Statutory liquidity ratio

solution:
The correct answer is __**1/ Cash Reserve Ratio.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The money multiplier can be expressed as **1/ Cash Reserve Ratio.**
 
• The money multiplier is the amount of **money created by commercial banks **for a given fixed amount of base money and reserve ratio.
 
• An increase in a **cash reserve ratio prevents the banks from lending more money and reduces the money multiplier.**
 
 
• An increase in the banking habit of the population will increase lending, thereby will lead to more deposits in the banking system, hence increasing the money multiplier.
 
• Even if there is an increase in the population of the country, the money multiplier in an economy does not necessarily increase. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 **The statutory liquidity ratio **means ensuring that commercial banks are solvent and that they invest in government securities.

 
 
• 
 By sapping market liquidity, an increase in the SLR limits the bank's ability to lend while also aiding in the management of inflation.
 
 
• 
 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) utilizes the statutory liquidity ratio as a tool for its monetary policy to evaluate the liquidity available to banks.
